clue.text: Olden (i.e. retro) housing owner? No

indicators.note: the opening words house the solution, holding it inside their run of letters

blocks.note: read straight through, ignoring the brackets and full stops

explanation.surface: Someone harks back to the old days of home ownership, then flatly refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is olDEN I.E. Retro. The definition reads 'not an owner-upper': someone who will not own up is a DENIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up means admitting; a person who answers no to admitting something is one who denies it.

clue.text: Newspaper essential to free choice?

indicators.note: something essential to a phrase sits at its core, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A paper argues that a free press is vital to people choosing freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is frEE CHOice. Many British local papers are called the Echo, such as the Liverpool Echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is a common title for a regional newspaper, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: If one has name and number taken by copper, ring Guardian – 'Blameless!'

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter
in this paper's puzzles the Guardian refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: Someone whose name and number are taken by a policeman phones the newspaper to protest innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is both the police officer of the surface and the metal Cu; the Guardian, where this puzzle runs, is US.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocuous strictly means harmless, and a harmless person or act gives no cause for blame or offence.

clue.text: One in three casually put back on the burner?

indicators.note: the single item is placed inside the word that follows
done casually means done loosely and without order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A third of something is carelessly returned to the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm food again you put it back on the hob, so the phrase describes the verb exactly.

clue.text: King doing a U-turn on primary headwear

indicators.note: a U-turn sends you back the way you came, so the short word that follows runs backwards

blocks.note: chief and primary both mean main

explanation.surface: A monarch reverses a policy concerning the main type of hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a joining word, but it is the short word for 'concerning', and that is what turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerchief is a square of cloth worn over the head, a traditional piece of headwear.

clue.text: Thousand things to be settled, going forward – that covers the whole board

indicators.note: things still to be settled are not yet in their final order, so these letters must be arranged

blocks.note: K is short for a thousand

explanation.surface: A long list of unresolved matters is being advanced, in the manner of a boardroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard: a knight's progress, or knight's tour, is a route on which a knight visits every square once.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight's route lands on every square of the chessboard, so it covers all of it.

clue.text: Car part needs right sort of aid (roll-up)

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the word is rearranged
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the list word runs backwards

blocks.note: a roll and a rota are both lists of names

explanation.surface: A motorist's component needs help of the right kind, like a cigarette roll-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll-up' looks like a hand-rolled cigarette; it is a roll (ROTA) going up in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The radiator cools a vehicle's engine, so it is one component of the motor.

clue.text: Firm confiscates ball collection

indicators.note: confiscating means seizing and holding, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: firm and hard both mean solid
a ball is round like the letter

explanation.surface: A company seizes a set of balls, perhaps from a neighbour's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a company; it is the adjective HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stored-up stock or stash of things, a kind of accumulated collection.

clue.text: One isn't this emphatically less sensitive

blocks.note: even adds emphasis, as in 'even better'

explanation.surface: Someone protests strongly that they are not this, and are less touchy than you think.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is the comparative of numb, not the noun it then becomes.
explanation.definitionFit: The integer 1 cannot be divided by two, so it fails to be a member of that class of integers.

clue.text: Major city's society put up hospital with computer technology

blocks.note: to hang a picture is to put it up

explanation.surface: A big metropolis's elite build a hospital equipped with computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is China's largest city by population, a leading port and financial centre.

clue.text: It's routinely filled by a minor agent with relief, perversely!

definitions.text: It's routinely filled by a minor

indicators.note: acting perversely means going the opposite way, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent
aid and relief both mean help

explanation.surface: A junior salesperson keeps filling something with a sense of relief, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The minor is a baby, not a junior agent; DIAPER is the American word for a nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy is regularly soiled by an infant, and the minor in the clue is that infant.

clue.text: Cold outbreak between flights here prompts emergency action

blocks.note: abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
an outbreak of spots on the skin
a landing is the level space between flights of stairs

explanation.surface: A spreading infection between plane journeys forces an emergency measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Flights look like air travel, but they are flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing an aircraft down hard in a crisis is an emergency manoeuvre taken by a pilot.

clue.text: Human tornado with hip replacement!

indicators.note: replacement suggests parts swapped about, so the letters are put in new positions

explanation.surface: A whirlwind of a person who has just had an artificial hip fitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid means resembling people in form, a near synonym of manlike or humanlike.

clue.text: Reinforced housing data

indicators.note: the word before contains the solution within its own letters

explanation.surface: Strengthened accommodation is described in some figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, which is what facts and figures are.

clue.text: Who's bothered about mite when performance starts?

indicators.note: bothered means stirred up, so the preceding word's letters are jumbled
about means around, so the following word is turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Nobody minds a tiny insect once the curtain goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Showtime is the moment a show is due to begin, the hour a performance gets under way.

clue.text: To toughen up, partook of mild

blocks.note: to temper steel is to harden it
to partake of food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone drank a mild ale to steel themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a British beer, so 'partook of mild' reads as drinking; mild is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate is moderate, free of extremes, which is what mild weather means.

clue.text: Division, about to go over Georgia, turned back

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the state's abbreviation runs backwards
going over something can mean covering it, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A split happens as someone is about to cross Georgia, then turns round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' works as covering: the departure word wraps around the reversed state, all after the 'about' letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or separation, as in a sharp political divide between groups.

clue.text: Artist's mountain resort

blocks.note: first meaning: James McNeill ..., the American painter
second meaning: a ski resort in British Columbia, Canada

explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive, as if the painter owned a resort; it means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistler painted the famous portrait of his mother, and a Canadian ski village bears the same name.

clue.text: Look, one's in pieces

indicators.note: something in pieces is broken up, so its letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: what belongs to one is mine

explanation.surface: Someone points out that their possession has been smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a person's bearing or expression, the appearance or air they present.

clue.text: Snake – shot it with a tracking movement

indicators.note: shot means wrecked, as in 'my nerves are shot', so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a camera pans to follow a subject

explanation.surface: A wildlife film-maker shoots a serpent with a sweeping camera move.
explanation.walkthrough: The taipan is a highly venomous Australian snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is an Australian elapid, one of the most venomous serpents in the world.

clue.text: Stiff tongue that reveals your true feelings?

blocks.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse

explanation.surface: An awkward way of speaking that betrays how you really feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff tongue' suggests stilted speech; it is a corpse plus a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture and gesture give away unspoken emotions, so this nonverbal signalling exposes real feelings.

clue.text: 'Theatre in the blue' over a long time

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other
turned over means flipped, so the whole combination is read backwards

blocks.note: No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese theatre

explanation.surface: A quoted title, like a festival called Theatre in the Blue, that ran for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Yonks is British slang for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonks is informal British slang meaning ages, an extremely lengthy period.

clue.text: Fellow Brummie is going to charge

blocks.note: Brummie is the setter, so the setter is going to is I'll

explanation.surface: A man from Birmingham is about to make an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is this puzzle's setter, and also the word for someone from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a glass or a gun is to load it, which is a sense of the verb meaning to make full.

clue.text: Optical feature's nucleus almost within reach – almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so each word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Something about the eye's centre is nearly within grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'almost's apply: one cuts the last letter from the centre word, one from the reach word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front layer of the eye, a part of the visual organ.

clue.text: Weight of detailed, misshapen rocks

indicators.note: de-tailed means having the tail removed, so the next word loses its last letter
something on the rocks is wrecked, so the shortened word is shuffled

explanation.surface: The heft of carefully worked, oddly shaped stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as intricate; it means de-tailed, losing a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To give weight to a point is to stress it, so weight here means importance or stress.

clue.text: Epic character extracted dues – so, yes, heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the last word goes
letters extracted are pulled out and rearranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary hero cruelly squeezed payments out of people.
explanation.walkthrough: Odysseus is the hero of Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the wandering king of Ithaca, protagonist of Homer's long heroic poem.

clue.text: Lionel's cracking surface decoration

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so the name's letters fall into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A man named Lionel does excellent ornamental finishing work.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to ornament engraved silver and gold.
